question: The first known rules of Kabaddi were framed in which Indian state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first known rules of Kabaddi were framed in **Maharashtra**, India.
 
• Kabaddi, as a sport, has deep roots in Indian culture and has been played informally across regions for centuries.
 
• In 1921, a structured format and rules were introduced to Kabaddi during the All India Kabaddi Tournament in Maharashtra.
 
• The state of Maharashtra played a pivotal role in popularizing Kabaddi and transforming it into a competitive sport.
 
• The Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI) was later formed in 1950 to further regulate and promote Kabaddi at the national level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Origin of Kabaddi:**

 
 
• Kabaddi is believed to have originated in ancient India, with references in historical texts such as the Mahabharata.
 
• It was traditionally played to develop physical strength and stamina, particularly in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Types of Kabaddi:**
 
 
• There are different formats of Kabaddi, including Circle Style Kabaddi, Standard Style Kabaddi, and Beach Kabaddi.
 
• Standard Style Kabaddi is the format played in international tournaments, including the Asian Games and Pro Kabaddi League.
 
 
 
• **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL):**
 
 
• The Pro Kabaddi League, launched in 2014, is a professional Kabaddi league in India that has significantly contributed to the sport’s popularity.
 
• It follows the Standard Style Kabaddi format and features teams from various Indian cities.
 
 
 
• **Global Reach of Kabaddi:**
 
 
• Kabaddi is now played in over 30 countries worldwide, with nations like Iran, South Korea, and Pakistan being prominent competitors.
 
• The International Kabaddi Federation (IKF) governs Kabaddi globally, organizing events like the Kabaddi World Cup.
